unit.why: A single narrative: a woman who cannot become ritually pure goes to the Seer of Lublin, who sends her to the Maggid of Kozienice; on her return the Seer interprets the amulet she received.

stories.start_quote: נודע ממגידי אמת כי אשה אחת
stories.summary_en: A woman with a persistent bleeding (niddah) problem is sent by the Seer of Lublin to the Maggid of Kozienice, who gives her an amulet reading 'וטהרה ממקור דמיה' with the first mem erased; the Seer explains that the erasure was deliberate, so that her source would be purified without being left without blood.

tags.why: The Maggid writes an amulet, and its wording is the story's point.
A bodily ailment that remedies failed to cure is healed by a tzaddik.
The woman travels to the tzaddikim with her request.

quotes: ואמר לה שתסע לקאזניץ להסבא קדישא
tags.why: The Seer sends her on to another tzaddik.
The woman is the central actor and travels on her own initiative.
The laws of niddah purity frame her problem.

quotes: כמה הפליא לעשות בזה שמחק המ"ם ראשונה
tags.why: The precise erasure in the amulet acts as a wondrous cure.
Her impurity prevents marital relations with her husband.
One tzaddik interprets and admires another tzaddik's power.
The hidden meaning of the erased letter is recognized only later.
